chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥammād ibn ʿUthmān, from al-Ḥalabī, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about one who did not catch the khutbah on Friday. He said: He prays two rakʿahs. But if the prayer has passed him and he did not catch it, then let him pray four. And he said: If you catch the Imam before he bows in the last rakʿah, then you have caught the prayer. But if you catch him after he has bowed, then it is ẓuhr, four rakʿahs.

key_terms.أَرْبَعًا: four units of prayer, referring here to ẓuhr prayer
key_terms.الرَّكْعَةَ الْأَخِيرَةَ: the final unit of the congregational prayer
key_terms.الظُّهْرُ: the noon prayer, performed as four rakʿahs when Jumuʿah is not caught
key_terms.الْإِمَامَ: the prayer leader in the congregational Friday prayer
key_terms.الْخُطْبَةَ: the Friday sermon delivered before the congregational prayer
key_terms.رَكْعَتَيْنِ: two units of prayer, the form of Jumuʿah prayer
key_terms.يَوْمَ الْجُمُعَةِ: the day of Friday, the occasion of Jumuʿah prayer

ai.seo_question: If someone misses the Friday khutbah or joins late, does he still pray Jumuʿah or ẓuhr?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the ruling for one who misses the Friday khutbah or joins the Friday prayer late. If he reaches the Imam before the bowing of the final rakʿah, he has caught the Friday prayer; otherwise, he must pray ẓuhr as four rakʿahs.
